NoteTexAccessor::strip_preamble¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note NoteTexAccessor::strip_preamble() const

Isolate A Complete Document Body¶

strip_preamble() returns the source between the first complete exact \begin{document} and the next complete exact \end{document}. Bytes before the opener and after the closer are discarded. Use it when a full document must be reduced to its authored body before command extraction or conversion. Use strip_pkgs() when only package and document-class calls should be removed while all other source remains, or strip_metadata() for title-page declarations alone.

Whitespace is permitted between begin or end and the balanced {document} group, and around document inside that group. Matching is exact, case-sensitive, and lexical: escaped tags and longer control words do not form boundaries. Both boundaries are required. If either is absent or malformed, the entire cell is returned unchanged rather than guessing where authored content ends. The extracted body is trimmed at its outer ASCII whitespace; internal line endings and all nested environments remain byte-for-byte intact.

The operation is out-of-place and shape preserving. A document with an empty body yields an empty Text cell, not an absent lane. Undefined state propagates; defined non-Text input rejects. The implementation makes a linear scan and does not parse, compile, or validate the document body.

Example 1: Extract A Body And Retain Nested Source¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note(
    R"(\documentclass{article}
\begin { document }
Body \begin{figure}x\end{figure}
\end{document}
trailer)");
std::cout << source.tex().strip_preamble() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"Body \\begin{figure}x\\end{figure}"

Example 2: Incomplete And Escaped Boundaries Are Loss-Preserving¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(head \begin{document}body)",
    R"(\\begin{document}escaped\\end{document})",
    "plain body"});
std::cout << source.tex().strip_preamble() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["head \\begin{document}body", "\\\\begin{document}escaped\\\\end{document}", "plain body"]

Example 3: Empty Bodies And Matrix Shape¶

const auto grid = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{R"(h\begin{document}A\end{document}t)",
                             "plain", R"(\begin{document}\end{document})", ""},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << grid.tex().strip_preamble() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["A", "plain"],
  ["", ""]
]

Example 4: Idempotence And Type Boundaries¶

const auto once = pluss::make_note(
    R"(head\begin{document}body\end{document}tail)")
    .tex().strip_preamble();
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "idempotent="
          << ((once == once.tex().strip_preamble()).all().bool_item())
          << " undefined="
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().strip_preamble().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1}).tex().strip_preamble();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

idempotent=true undefined=false
Int64: rejected
